editions.title: Jeff Bezos Bids On Liverpool FC

stories.headline: Consortium Including Tech Billionaires Seeks Minority Stake In Liverpool FC
body: British businessman Amit Bhatia leads a wealthy investor group that includes Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin.
The group is negotiating to buy a share of the English soccer team from its current owner, American sports company Fenway Sports Group.
This marks the team's first outside funding since investment firm Dynasty Equity purchased a three percent share for nearly $200M in 2023.

stories.headline: Fenway Sports Group Buys Boston Team In New Women's Pro Golf League
body: Global sports firm Fenway Sports Group bought Boston Common Golf, one of five founding teams in the new WTGL women's league.
This marks the firm's first team ownership in women's golf, building on prior investments in the league's creator, TMRW Sports.
The new league launches this fall in Florida, featuring top professional players to help expand global access to the sport.

stories.headline: Tampa Changes Funding Strategy For The $2.3B Tampa Bay Rays Ballpark
body: City leaders dropped plans to use $180M in public taxes to fund a new stadium for the Tampa Bay Rays baseball team.
The revised plan uses taxes generated by commercial development directly around the stadium, avoiding the use of broader public funds.
Total public spending is capped at $976M, meaning the team must cover remaining costs and finalize agreements quickly for a 2029 opening.

stories.headline: NFL Preseason Opener Reaches Five-Year Viewership High
body: The preseason football broadcast on television network NBC averaged 6.99M viewers, a slight increase over last year.
Despite featuring two struggling professional football franchises, the matchup was the most-watched exhibition opener since 2021.
This massive turnout proves NFL practice games still draw larger crowds than most regular-season baseball, basketball, and hockey events.

stories.headline: Comcast And Disney Reach Agreement To Restore NFL Channels
body: Major cable provider Comcast agreed to new fees with entertainment giant Disney, ending a three-month blackout of NFL Network and NFL RedZone.
The agreement restores football television access for Comcast's 10.67M cable subscribers just before the preseason games officially begin.
Disney gained distribution rights to these channels in February by giving the NFL a 10% ownership stake in its sports network, ESPN.

stories.headline: Major Football Confederations Continue To Demand Resignation Of FIFA President Gianni Infantino
body: Regional governing bodies UEFA, Concacaf, and the AFC issued a joint letter demanding Infantino step down over a controversial private investment plan.
The failed proposal would have allowed private investors to buy commercial stakes in major global tournaments like the World Cup.
The groups are demanding an independent review of his actions, though Infantino still retains support from African and South American football bodies.

stories.headline: Buffalo Bills Fans Discover Obstructed Views Inside New $2.2B Stadium
body: Fans at the Buffalo Bills' new $2.2B NFL stadium went viral sharing photos of railings and stairs obstructing their views of the field.
The professional football team made $260M selling 53K seat licenses using digital previews, leaving some fans feeling misled by the actual physical sightlines.
The franchise secured $850M in public funding to build the venue and now has six weeks to address complaints before its home opener.

stories.headline: Rare Michael Jordan Autographed Card Box Sells For $1.48M At Auction
body: Trading card company Upper Deck auctioned this one-of-a-kind sealed box containing the basketball legend's highly coveted rookie cards.
The $1.48M sale price is surprisingly lower than a single signed rookie card, which sold for a record $2.7M recently.
Collectors spent over $68M on the star's individual cards in early 2026.

stories.headline: New York Yankees Secure $2.6B Deal With Apollo Sports Capital
body: Investment firm Apollo Sports Capital provided a $2.6B mix of debt and equity to help the baseball team pay off loans and expand.
The Steinbrenner family will retain full control of the team, while the CEO of Apollo joins the parent company's board.
This cash infusion supports the franchise, highly valued at $8.5B, and its other properties like sports networks and soccer clubs.

stories.headline: Trinity Investments Sells Grande Lakes Orlando Resort For $1.38B
body: Hospitality firm Ryman Hospitality Properties bought the Florida estate, marking the largest non-gaming US resort sale on record.
Real estate firm Trinity Investments purchased the site for $870M in 2018, earning a huge profit after upgrading the property.
The 409-acre complex features a Ritz-Carlton, a JW Marriott, and a championship golf course, driving its high valuation.

stories.headline: Netflix Halts Second Season Of SEC College Football Docuseries
body: The Southeastern Conference, a major college sports league, and streaming giant Netflix will not film a new season this year.
The debut season attracted 3M views, trailing behind the 5.6M viewers drawn by similar football shows on the platform.
League officials stated the original plan was always to film one single season to test the waters before reassessing.

stories.headline: Tottenham Hotspur Owners Explore Bid For London NBA Europe Team
body: The Lewis family, owners of English soccer club Tottenham Hotspur, partnered with two veteran American sports-investing families for a joint bid.
NBA Europe is a proposed continental basketball league launching in 2027 that will feature 12 permanent franchises in major cities.
The group faces stiff competition from tech billionaire Nikesh Arora, whose rival investor consortium is preparing a bid exceeding $1B.

stories.headline: New Basketball League Project B Adopts Global Gender Rules Amid WNBA Criticism
body: Project B, an upcoming global basketball league co-founded by former star Alana Beard, criticized WNBA leadership for failing to clarify gender policies.
The new league will follow strict International Olympic Committee guidelines that currently ban transgender women from competing in female sports categories.
This proactive move gives players clear rules while the WNBA continues to review its own vague eligibility guidelines amid growing public debate.

stories.headline: Donald Trump Backs FIFA President Gianni Infantino Against Growing Calls For Resignation
body: Gianni Infantino, president of global soccer group FIFA, faces major backlash over a recently failed proposal to sell stakes in the World Cup.
US President Trump defended Infantino's track record, highlighting the recent completion of a historic $15B revenue cycle for the sport.
Trump’s public support directly opposes the US soccer federation and multiple international soccer bodies that are demanding immediate leadership changes.

stories.headline: Unregulated US Online Gambling Reaches $97.4B Despite Legal Market Expansion
body: The illegal sector captured 77% of total US online gambling revenue last year, dwarfing the $28.3B generated by state-regulated platforms.
Data shows that legalizing betting did not eliminate unlicensed offshore sites, but instead caused overall gambling demand to surge nationwide.
The Campaign for Fairer Gambling, an industry advocacy group, is urging states to pause new expansions until enforcement against illegal operators improves.

stories.headline: Los Angeles Lakers Sold To Bob Iger And Joshua Kushner For $12.5B
body: Former Disney CEO Bob Iger and investor Joshua Kushner are buying the basketball team from Dodgers owner Mark Walter.
The $12.5B purchase sets a new professional sports record, easily surpassing the team's $10B valuation from 14 months ago.
Despite the ownership change, current team executive Jeanie Buss will keep her leadership role for at least five years.

stories.headline: J.P. Morgan Issues Cautious Outlook On FanDuel Parent Flutter Entertainment Amid Falling Market Share
body: FanDuel, Flutter's primary US sports betting brand, saw its market share drop from 47% to 39% following the departure of two top executives.
The business faces rising competition from unregulated prediction markets, which allow users to wager on events without navigating traditional sports betting taxes.
These US struggles, along with international issues like a steep UK tax hike to 40%, caused Flutter’s stock to fall 68% from historic highs.

stories.headline: Capital One Extends Washington Arena Naming Rights Through 2047
body: The 20-year renewal keeps the bank's name on the home of the NBA's Wizards and NHL's Capitals.
Owner Monumental Sports & Entertainment is halfway through a $1B-plus renovation, with $500M funded by Washington D.C.
Capital One cardholders will get a dedicated arena entrance and discounts across the venue under the deal.

stories.headline: DP World Tour To Reinstate Fines And Suspensions For LIV Golfers In 2027
body: The DP World Tour, a major European golf circuit, will resume penalizing players who compete in the rival LIV Golf league starting in 2027.
This policy change follows LIV's new plan to offer players equity, which officials fear will discourage full participation in European events.
The reinstated fines threaten the 2027 Ryder Cup hopes of European athletes, as the tour controls team selection for the prestigious tournament.

stories.headline: WNBA Faces Potential Legal Battles Over Vague Gender Eligibility Rules
body: Former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White sparked debate by threatening to exploit undefined gender rules for the 2027 draft.
The current labor agreement requires players to be women but lacks a clear definition, leaving the WNBA vulnerable to workplace discrimination lawsuits.
While only about 10 of 500K college athletes are transgender, legal experts advise the league and union to clarify entry requirements.

stories.headline: Federal Regulator Allows Prediction Market Kalshi To Bypass New York Gambling Ban
body: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission, a US federal agency, used emergency authority to keep the platform online despite state objections.
New York sued Kalshi for illegal gambling, seeking $36B in penalties because the platform bypasses local taxes and underage betting limits.
The outcome will determine if betting on real-world events should be regulated as a federal financial trade or a state-level casino game.

stories.headline: Dallas Cowboys Ranked Most Valuable NFL Franchise At $15.5B
body: The professional football team Dallas Cowboys retained their top ranking with a $15.5B valuation, growing 21% despite missing the playoffs.
The Seattle Seahawks, the recent championship winners, achieved the largest growth by jumping 46% to reach a $9.6B total value.
Even the lowest-valued franchise, the Cincinnati Bengals, saw tremendous financial success by increasing their worth 35% to hit $7.4B.

stories.headline: $12.5B Los Angeles Lakers Sale And NBA Title Drive Record Results For MSG Sports
body: Investors Bob Iger and Josh Kushner are buying the Los Angeles Lakers for $12.5B, boosting shares of Knicks owner MSG Sports.
MSG Sports reported a record $1.15B in annual revenue, fueled by the New York Knicks winning their first NBA title in 53 years.
To increase shareholder value, MSG Sports plans to separate the Knicks from its hockey team, the Rangers, by the end of October.

stories.headline: Philadelphia 76ers Secure Maximum NBA TV Exposure After Signing LeBron James
body: Basketball superstar LeBron James signed with the Philadelphia 76ers, boosting their national TV games from 14 to a league maximum of 34.
Similarly, the major trade sending star player Giannis Antetokounmpo to the Miami Heat increased that franchise's showcase games from five to 25.
Meanwhile, the Los Angeles Lakers will remain at 34 national TV games given the star power of Luka Doncic and their broad brand recognition.

stories.headline: Formula E Signs Global Streaming Deal With Disney+ To Expand Audience
body: The electric racing series will stream in 144 countries on Disney+ starting in 2026, prioritizing global audience growth over exclusive broadcast fees.
US coverage will also feature on major sports network ESPN+, filling a live racing gap after the network recently lost Formula One rights.
This unprecedented partnership taps into the streaming giant's 131.6M subscribers and will sit alongside free local TV channels to maximize total viewership.

stories.headline: Baseball Star Shohei Ohtani Plans To Stay With Dodgers Even If Team Is Sold
body: Mark Walter, CEO of investment firm Guggenheim Partners, is under federal investigation and recently sold the Los Angeles Lakers, sparking Dodgers sale rumors.
Ohtani's 10-year, $700M contract includes a rare clause allowing him to quit if Walter leaves the baseball franchise.
Sources say the superstar will stay regardless because the management successfully built a winning roster using his deferred salary.

stories.headline: NFL Quarterback Jayden Daniels Issues Cease-And-Desist To LSU Over Jersey Number
body: The conflict started after Louisiana State University let a current player wear the jersey number Daniels used to win the 2023 Heisman Trophy.
Daniels’ legal team claims the school’s right to profit from his image has expired and demanded the university return his replica trophy.
LSU head coach Lane Kiffin defended the reassignment, stating the student was promised the specific number when he committed to the school.

stories.headline: Media Publisher The Arena Group Rebrands As Paradium.AI Amid Financial Struggles
body: The Arena Group, publisher of Athlon Sports magazine, rebranded to Paradium.AI and acquired artificial intelligence tools to mass-produce digital content.
This pivot aims to rescue the financially distressed firm, which currently carries $98M in debt and recently saw quarterly revenue halve to $22M.
Management hopes these tech upgrades will lower expenses by replacing traditional salaried writers with independent freelancers paid only when their articles generate traffic.

editions.title: Jeff Bezos Buys 30% Stake In Liverpool

stories.headline: Jeff Bezos And Investor Group Buy 30% Stake In Liverpool FC
body: The group bought roughly 30% of the team, led by soccer executive Amit Bhatia alongside Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin.
Fenway Sports Group retains majority ownership and control, securing a huge profit on a franchise that previously sold a 3% stake for $200M.
The deal adds no immediate cash for new players, instead relying on the investors' technology backgrounds to help grow the team's global brand.

stories.headline: NBA Star LeBron James Launches A YouTube Golf Channel
body: The channel's premiere video features a 96-minute Scotland golf trip with former Cleveland Cavaliers teammates to celebrate their 2016 championship.
This launch follows the 41-year-old athlete's recent free-agency move to the Philadelphia 76ers on a two-year, $8M contract.
James hopes this expanding media portfolio will inspire inner-city youth to access country clubs and learn the game of golf.

stories.headline: Burnley Football Club Replaces Finotive One With Vertu Motors As Shirt Sponsor
body: The soccer team abruptly canceled its one-year deal with retail trading firm Finotive One just two months after signing it.
UK automotive retailer Vertu Motors immediately stepped in to become the new main sponsor for the upcoming season.
Fans who already bought jerseys with the old sponsor logo can request a full refund or exchange them for updated shirts.

stories.headline: MSG Sports Files Paperwork To Separate The Rangers And Knicks
body: MSG Sports, the parent company of both teams, filed official registration documents to split its professional basketball and hockey businesses.
The proposed spin-off will create two distinct, independent companies for the NBA's New York Knicks and the NHL's New York Rangers.
This corporate separation allows each sports franchise to operate independently and attract focused financial investments.

stories.headline: Women's Tennis Association Hires Secretive Firm For Mandatory Genetic Sex Testing
body: The professional tennis league hired Colorado-based Phuel Sports Science to enforce a new rule requiring all female athletes to pass a genetic sex screening.
Phuel usually sells fitness blood tests for up to $1K, but its leaders are concealing their identities despite managing this highly sensitive medical data.
The mandatory screenings will begin in 2026 to align with Olympic guidelines regulating transgender athlete eligibility in elite women's sports.

stories.headline: New Zealand Football Withdraws Support For FIFA President Gianni Infantino
body: The withdrawal follows a controversial, now-scrapped plan by Infantino, leader of global soccer governing body FIFA, to sell tournament shares to private investors.
New Zealand's sports organization cited a breakdown in trust and demanded an independent review to improve transparency within the global administration.
Multiple regional soccer groups have also dropped their support ahead of a November deadline to nominate a rival candidate for the next election.

stories.headline: Trading Card Maker Panini Accuses Rival Fanatics Of Stealing Confidential Licensing Data
body: Panini alleges sports retailer Fanatics used stolen financial details, like royalty rates, to win exclusive trading card deals with major sports leagues.
The lawsuit claims the basketball players union and OneTeam Partners, a sports licensing group, conspired with Fanatics to monopolize the market.
Fanatics strongly denies the claims, stating that Panini is just lashing out at former partners who chose a better business model.

stories.headline: Judge Dismisses Charles Oakley's Assault Lawsuit Against Madison Square Garden
body: A federal judge ruled that former NBA star Charles Oakley lacked evidence proving Madison Square Garden security assaulted him during a 2017 game.
This defeat follows a previous order requiring Oakley to pay the arena company $642K in legal fees for failing to preserve relevant text messages.
While Oakley plans to appeal, the sports and entertainment company now intends to sue his legal team for pursuing a frivolous nine-year lawsuit.
